decision.case_state: Inbound call handled. Caller identifies as Priya Shah, tenant at P-203 (Flat 9, 3 Amhurst Road). Name and DOB match the CRM tenant record T-1003. Contact number does not match. No maintenance ticket involved. Contact-number discrepancy and legacy record conflict are noted for ops.

next_actions.action: Logged the inbound call and its outcome on the record.
Recorded a note on the property flagging the legacy Fixflo conflict and the unverified phone number, for ops to confirm the tenant's preferred phone on the next routine contact.

boundaries: Name and DOB match does not prove the caller's identity beyond the CRM record; the number used does not match the one on file.
No contact details, tenancy dates or bank details were changed.
The legacy Fixflo row was not used for any fact given to the caller.
This does not confirm the tenancy end date. It is periodic with no fixed end date, so the tenant's own written notice governs when they leave.
remaining_work: Ops to confirm the tenant's preferred phone number and update CRM if it has changed (owner: ops/lettings).
Ops to clean up the legacy Fixflo row for Flat 9 (P. Shah-Mehta, +447700900166) so it is not used for contact (owner: data quality).
missing_info: Confirmation from the tenant of her preferred contact number (the call came from a number not on file).
Whether the tenancy is periodic from 2026-01-10 or was a fixed term before 1 May 2026 (not in the record).
decision.summary: The caller gave the name Priya Shah and DOB 21/07/1998, both matching the CRM tenant T-1003 at P-203. I logged the call and told her the tenancy is periodic with no fixed end date (2 months' written notice to leave) and her £1,903 deposit is held in DPS, per CRM. The CRM is authoritative over the legacy Fixflo row, which lists a different person who left in 2025, and I flagged the unverified phone number for ops.

answers.question: 1. Which record do you treat as authoritative and why?
answers.answer: The CRM record (dwelly_crm, T-1003). It is the highest-priority source in the data_quality ordering, it is current and active, and its name, DOB and tenancy start agree with the caller. The legacy Fixflo export (imported 2026-03 from an acquisition, not maintained) lists 'P. Shah-Mehta' with a different phone, status ended and move-out 2025-11-30. That row looks like a previous occupant, so I did not use it for any fact.

answers.question: 2. Is the caller verified? What can you tell her?
answers.answer: Partly. Her name and DOB match the CRM record, which is the identity check the policy requires. But she called from a number that is not on file (caller ID +447700900177, and she said it is a work phone; CRM has +447700900103), so this is a hint, not proof. I shared only general information: the tenancy is periodic with no fixed end date, and she would give 2 months' written notice; the deposit is £1,903 held in DPS per the CRM. I did not give any balance, ticket or personal data beyond that.

answers.question: 3. What do you do about the conflicting records?
answers.answer: I logged the call and added an internal note on P-203 recording the conflict: the legacy row is treated as a previous occupant and not used for contact or tenancy facts, and the unverified number is flagged. I changed no contact details. Ops should confirm her preferred phone on the next routine contact, and the legacy row should be cleaned up.

Caller ID +447700900177 and her stated work phone match neither record. Treated as an unverified contact, not used for identity.
assumptions: The legacy Fixflo row is a previous occupant of the same flat, not the same tenant under a different name.
The 2026-01-10 tenancy start is the current tenancy and the deposit figure is current.
